departments.title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
departments.summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.
notes: PLAYCRAFT re-assessed the existing build for this report (not recorded in the Game Quality History).
departments.next: Run PLAYCRAFT on this game (studiocraft playcraft_pass) to measure how it plays.

quality.label: Gameplay quality
quality.source: PLAYCRAFT's own overall score from the Game Quality History
criteria: 10 categories (core gameplay, game feel, controls, progression, difficulty, player experience, replayability, technical, presentation, mobile), genre-weighted
Each criterion pass/partial/fail, weighted by evidence: verified 1, observed 0.85, inferred 0.45
A category with no played (verified/observed) evidence is capped at 70; untested criteria count for nothing
quality.why: Run PLAYCRAFT on this game (studiocraft playcraft_pass) to measure how it plays.

departments.title: PIXELCRAFT — visual quality, UI/UX and interface efficiency
departments.summary: Audits the rendered application (not its source) in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13, desktop, narrow, tablet and landscape viewports: discovers its screens, captures screenshots, measures spacing, alignment, typography, touch targets, control consistency, safe areas, overflow, layout shift, hover/pressed/focus/disabled states, runs axe-core and user journeys (taps, depth, confirmations, feedback time). Scores Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency (100 each) from evidence, with coverage and confidence reported separately; every finding has screen, viewport, selector, measurements, severity, an annotated screenshot and a fix. verify replays the same routes, viewports and journeys, diffs screenshots, proves fixes and refuses score gains from lost coverage. Works on React, Vite, Next.js, static sites and browser games (HTML overlays). Never modifies the app.
departments.applies_because: PIXELCRAFT audits the rendered HTML UI of apps, sites and games

findings.evidence: Fixed or sticky bars cover 100% of the phone screen height, leaving little room for content.
findings.recommendation: Shrink or hide bars on scroll, or merge them.

findings.title: Accessibility: All page content should be contained by landmarks
findings.evidence: axe-core rule region (best practice): All page content should be contained by landmarks.
findings.recommendation: See https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/region?application=axeAPI — Fix any of the following:   Some page content is not contained by landmarks

findings.title: Content disappears at one screen size
findings.evidence: At narrow, 'home' shows only 70% of the words other sizes show; hidden content on phones is a common source of 'where did it go?'.
findings.recommendation: Reflow content instead of hiding it; move secondary content behind a disclosure rather than display: none.

findings.title: No hover state
findings.evidence: The pointer over this control changes nothing (colour, shadow, underline), so it does not signal that it is clickable.
findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: Spacing does not follow a consistent scale
findings.evidence: Paddings, gaps and margins use many unrelated values, so the rhythm between elements looks accidental rather than designed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a spacing scale (4/8-px steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) as tokens and replace one-off values with the nearest step.
